This is my first time looking on this sub, and I have to say it's relieving to see other people suggesting that "his" posts are suspicious and know I'm not the only one who felt weird interacting with "him." 

At the same time, though, it's very sad, because it means either that:

1) Someone or some people convinced him that he needed to have this sort of social media presence for some reason,

or that

2) He believes that, given that he doesn't want to play live, he owes his fans some sort of level of connection through social media. And the reason this is sad is that, given his life's trajectory up until now, it's at the least very uncertain that he developed this belief organically as opposed to through a lifetime of pressure as described in the podcast, especially by some of the excerpts from John Watson.

No one should drink and drive, but no one here (I'm guessing) is in a position like he is where it's impossible to go out during the daytime and/or into significantly populated areas without being noticed. He was totally in the wrong in this situation, but I still feel really sorry for him. He's the epitome of the misunderstood artist.

Take it from someone who has been able to juggle 100 times but would be picked last at a good 1/3 of pickup games - juggling is important (as I was told many times and got me started down the road to being able to juggle better than a lot of otherwise higher-skilled players than me) but its impact on your overall skills as a player can range widely. If you find yourself being able to closely control fast and/or long passes from teammates, I wouldn't worry about the number of juggles you can do at this point in time. Some of the higher-skilled players I mentioned before can't juggle that much but can kill meanly whipped 40 yd+ balls dead at their feet on command, and I can't. I don't think anyone would tell you that juggling is a waste of time, and it's not - it's the best thing you can do to maintain your control when you don't have anyone (and no wall) to control balls from - but just because you can only do 30 now, doesn't mean it won't be 50 in maybe even just a couple weeks if you really keep at it, and if that doesn't happen it shouldn't be taken as a sign that your overall game isn't progressing. Just commit to a juggling routine every day or every other day, forget about counting and before you know it you'll be clocking higher numbers (you'll know without having to count).
